messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — forecasting an Oct->Nov traffic bump (seasonal promotions). Need a pragmatic capacity hedge across H100 / H200 / L40S. Can we align on reservation vs spot mix in the next 48h?
aj: +1. Rough numbers? what's the target throughput we should optimize for (p50 latency target / tokens per sec)?
maria: Target p50 < 120ms for chat paths, sustain ~1.2M tokens/min system-wide at peak (very spiky). Rough GPU-hours calc I did: `~(1.2M tokens/min * 60 min * 24h) / 1.1M tokens/GPU-hour ~= 1000 GPU-hours/day` — ballpark.
cheng: Nice. A few constraints: H200 lead time is still long (vendors quoting 16-22 weeks), H100 ~10-14w if we commit, L40S is available via cloud immediately but higher per-token cost. APAC region has rack+cabinet lead delays too.
sara: For latency-sensitive chat I'd prefer L40S in-hosted pools close to users (APAC/US-EAST). Use H200 reserved capacity for bulk embedding/large-batch offline jobs. H100 can be our mid-cost/throughput option.
aj: Cost tradeoff numbers? If we reserve H200 we get ~35% discount vs on-demand, but west-coast supply is tight and we'd need minimum 6-month commit. Spot bursts on H100/L40S could cover spikes but not reliable.
infra-bot: [autoscaling snapshot] current utilization: us-east: 78%, eu-west: 62%, apac: 44%. Pending reservations: 120 H100 hours/day in queue.
cheng: Given lead times, we should 1) commit a baseline H200 pool for predictable batch capacity (enough for 60% of predicted batch), 2) keep H100 reserved small + spot burst allocation, 3) rely on L40S for low-latency regional frontends.
maria: Proposed numbers to review: baseline reserve = 600 GPU-hours/day H200 (covers 60% batch), H100 reserve = 150 GPU-hours/day, L40S on-demand pool = 300 GPU-hours/day for latency routes + 200 GPU-hours/day burst cap. Total trimmed for cost = ~1250 GPU-hours/day peak. Thoughts?
aj: That baseline seems reasonable. Two flags: shipping lead windows mean H200 commit must go out this week to hit Oct. Also need budget approval for the reserve commit.
sara: Also watch network egress saturations — last year's holiday spike we saw 35% higher cross-az traffic from prefix caching misses. If we run H200 in centralized region, add inter-region prefetch caches.
cheng: Agreed. Suggest adding KV prefix caching + aggressive short-lived soft cache to reduce inter-region egress. That reduces token duplication and saves GPU cycles.
maria: Action items: 1) aj to create procurement PO + vendor options (due EOD tomorrow), 2) cheng to draft reserve/spot mix config for autoscaler + fallback routing, 3) sara to run quick egress stress test on staging (script: `tools/loadgen --tokens 1e6 --burst 10s`). I'll schedule 30m sync tomorrow.
aj: On it. I'll also run cost sims with reserves vs purely on-demand (will post numbers).
infra-bot: [note] scheduled maintenance: us-east interconnect upgrade on 1930012900 (planned, 10m window) — might affect rolling upgrades.
maria: Good catch infra-bot — factor that into rollout timing. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
sara: One more: consider negotiation term length — 12mo vs 24mo changes unit price ~8%. I'll include that in procurement doc.
maria: Perfect. If no objections, proceed with procurement proposal and autoscaler draft tomorrow.
aj: No objections from me.
cheng: Fine here.
sara: fine.
maria: Closing thread — follow-ups in the meeting.
